title: Hadith close
hookLine: a science built on honesty, memory and travel

cards: Every saying in this block arrived the same way. Aisha telling what the Prophet ﷺ did at home. Jibril asking about ihsan.
Allah saying, whoever comes walking, I come running. Someone heard each one, held it, and handed it on, and someone else checked the one who handed it on. That's the whole block in a sentence.
A science built on honesty, on memory, and on travel. Today the block on hadith comes to a close, and the question is simple: across all those hands, how did the chain hold? Today: hadith close.

teach.h: LINK BY LINK, THE WHOLE BLOCK.
teach.b: Walk back down the block, link by link. A hadith: a report of what the Prophet said, did or approved. Sunnah and hadith: the way, carried.
Chain and text: who told whom, and the words, tested too. Sound, good, weak: graded with care. Many chains.
The science of men: who was he? Scholars on the road for a single report. Fabrications exposed, because they checked.

Then the books: Bukhari's sound collection, Muslim's, the four Sunan that complete the six books, the early collections of Malik and Ahmad, and the four books of the Shia with their own science of grading.
Then the sacred hadith, Jibril's questions, the women who taught the Sahih, memory, weak reports, the forties, commentary, and reading with a teacher. Three threads run through it all.
Honesty: the warnings against lying about the Prophet, taken seriously enough to build a whole craft of checking. Memory: words carried by heart, passed on just as they were heard.
Travel: students crossing long distances to sit in front of one narrator.
And one thing nobody could see from outside: every link was a person who could have cut a corner, and the narrators the critics trusted were the ones who didn't. So the chain held.
Not that every report is sound; this block spent whole days on weak and fabricated ones.
What held was the method. Name your source. Test it.
Say how sure you are. Tomorrow a new block begins: fiqh and the schools, what scholars built from the Qur'an and these reports.

how: Muslims often ask Allah's mercy for the scholars and narrators who carried the hadith, and students of hadith sometimes name their chain of teachers back to the Prophet when they teach.

o: the end of the hadith block: a science of honest, checked reports
the moment the last hadith collection was finally closed
a ruling that every report about the Prophet is sound

games.q: the hadith block — tap the pairs.
p: Bukhari, Muslim and the four Sunan

s: the block showed that every report about the Prophet is sound
it spent whole days on weak and fabricated reports. what held was the method of checking.
Shia scholars have their own collections and their own science of grading
the four books of the Shia, weighed by their own methods.
hadith critics judged the words only, never the people who carried them
the science of men asked of every narrator: who was he?

games.q: a friend says: if some hadith are weak and some were made up, why trust any of them? what does this block answer?
o: trust the method: name the source, test it, say how sure you are.
games.why: the scholars neither swallowed everything nor threw everything out. they graded what they carried, and the grading is the science.

practice: Bring to mind one hadith from this block that stayed with you, and walk back along its chain: the person or book you learned it from, the collector who checked it, the narrators before him, the companion who first heard it.
You don't need their names, just the line of people, hand to hand. If you pray, ask mercy for them; if you don't, let some thanks go to each pair of hands.

wordCard.voice: Hadith close. The end of the block on hadith: a science of reports built on honesty, memory and travel, that kept the Prophet's words and checked them, link by link. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the chain of narrators that carries a report.

carryVoice: Your line: the chain held. Hand to hand, all the way to you. The hadith block is done.
